title: Stage Spectral Cohort Insight
body:
Purpose
This doc is a compact results-and-insights brief from a cross-cohort end-to-end tracing exercise run across model variants and hardware types. Goal: explain where p50/p95/p99 comes from at the per-stage level, surface unusual spectral modes (multi-modal latency shapes), and recommend targeted mitigations we can experiment with in the next sprint.

Background and motivation
We observed an uptick in p99 across customer traffic the week of 2026-01-28. Host-level metrics (CPU/GPU util) were unimpressive; traces showed long tail stages that vary by request cohort. This investigation stitched together 45k sampled traces (1% sampling of production ingress) across two representative fleets: A100-backed gpt-medium-8k-fp16 and H100-backed llamaX-70B-q4. Traces include full stage timing (ingress proxy, auth/token, cache lookup, batching wait, model forward, kv-write, postprocess/serialize).

Methodology
- Sampling window: 2026-01-25 through 2026-02-01.
- Sample size: 45,123 traces after dedup and health-filter.
- Cohorts: prompt_length: short (<=128 tokens), medium (129-512), long (>512); cache: kv-hit vs kv-miss; coldstart flag: true if model instance started < 60s before request.
- Stage instrumentation: per-request timers emitted at ingress, post-auth, cache-lookup, batch-queue-enter, batch-queue-exit, model-exec-start, model-exec-end, kv-write, serializer-end.
- Aggregation: compute p50/p95/p99 per-stage and per-cohort; also compute contribution-to-endtime (stage_time / total_time) for each quantile.

Representative summary table (p50 / p95 / p99 in ms)
Note: numbers are cohort-aggregated medians across fleet variants; per-variant breakdown follows.

Stages                      | p50  | p95  | p99
------------------------------------------------
Ingress proxy               | 4    | 12   | 22
Auth/token                 | 3    | 9    | 15
KV cache lookup            | 6    | 45   | 110
Batching wait              | 2    | 75   | 340
Model forward              | 48   | 220  | 880
KV write (async)          | 1    | 6    | 12
Postprocess/serialize     | 5    | 20   | 48
Total (end-to-end)        | 70   | 420  | 1420

Per-variant spot-check (p99, ms)
- gpt-medium-8k-fp16 @ A100: 620 ms (p50 110, p95 340) - model forward dominates for medium+ long requests; p99 shows large batching-wait spikes on low-frequency sequences.
- llamaX-70B-q4 @ H100: 1,280 ms (p50 52, p95 400) - bimodal: many requests in p99 are kv-miss + coldstart + long prompt.

Cohort decompositions and interesting spectral modes
1) KV-hit short prompts (<=128 tokens): p99 ~ 210 ms. Breakdown: model_forward 60%, ingress+auth 6%, batching wait 12%, cache 8%. Conclusion: for small requests with cache hit, model-forward variability still large due to tail-QP scheduling on the H100 pool.

2) KV-miss medium prompts: p99 ~ 900 ms. Breakdown: cache lookup becomes reentrant (multiple backend hops) for misses; batching wait 25%, model_forward 55%. Localized spikes trace to backend K/V lookups timing out and falling back to slow store (trace ID examples below).

3) Coldstart long prompts: p99 > 2s for a small fraction (~0.6% of traces). Breakdown: coldstart stall (container warmup) 40-60% of total; model_forward 30%; batching wait 10%. These are real cold-container events that we need to address at scale.

Trace examples (anonymized IDs)
- trace-2026-01-29-7a2b: medium prompt, kv-miss -> shows repeated cache retries adding ~120ms before batch queue; model-forward p99 spike at 560ms.
- trace-2026-01-30-f1d3: long prompt + coldstart on H100, end-to-end 2.7s, warmup time 1.1s.
- trace-2026-01-27-4c9e: short prompt on A100 with batching microburst; batch-queue stall 310ms pushing p99.

Observations and hypotheses
- Batching wait is a large and variable contributor to p99 when request arrival pattern is bursty and queue thresholds are close to autoscale step thresholds. Hypothesis: the batching policy (max latency target vs batch size) is oscillating with autoscaler decisions.
- KV miss handling path has unexpected retries and a synchronous fallback to a remote store that adds significant jitter. Hypothesis: older SDK clients still call fallback path synchronously; we need to validate client-side library versions and ensure fallback is async.
- Coldstart-induced tails are concentrated in the H100 cluster following a deploy on 2026-01-26; hypothesis: the deploy launched instances with slower start-up due to model sharding configuration (external shard fetch blocking startup).
- Per-hardware differences indicate scheduling (kernel/pipeline warmup) effects beyond raw FLOPS: A100 shows fewer coldstart stalls for medium models, H100 shows higher variance especially on small batches.

Immediate recommended experiments (next 2 sprints)
1) Batching policy probe: create two canaries (one with conservative batch-latency target 25ms, one with aggressive 200ms) for gpt-medium on A100 and measure p95/p99 delta over 48h. Ticket: JIRA-ENG-5412.
2) Async-fallback rollout: change server-side KV client to async fallback path for misses (feature branch exists: PR #812). Run experiment for kv-miss cohort.
3) Coldstart mitigation: instrument image startup path to trace external shard fetch latency; run warmpool test to pre-warm 5% of H100 capacity during deploy windows.
4) Sampling policy tweak: increase sampling for long-prompt / kv-miss cohorts to 5% to get more signal for rare tail modes.

Longer-term suggestions
- Introduce per-stage SLOs and stage-level alerting (e.g., batch-queue p99 > 250ms for >5 minutes triggers an incident).
- Add a lightweight histogram-backed summary in the trace stream so downstream analytics can reconstruct multi-modal shapes without needing full trace replay for every sample.
- Evaluate model quantization/activation checkpoints for long prompt paths to reduce model-forward p99.

Action items and owners
- Marco: run the batch-policy canaries and report p50/p95/p99 delta (due 2026-02-26).
- Priya: implement async-kv-fallback in canary and coordinate PR #812 review (due 2026-02-16).
- Liam: instrument shard-fetch timing and prototype 5% warmpool (due 2026-03-05).
- Anika (me): increase trace sampling for target cohorts and assemble a small dashboard with cohort spectrograms for the weekly ops review (due 2026-02-19).

Open questions
- Are there legacy SDKs in the wild forcing synchronous fallback behavior? (Need telemetry from client versions.)
- Should we bias routing away from H100 for short prompts until we understand kernel scheduling variance?

Appendix: quick artifact links
- Canary config diff: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/compare/batch-canary
- PR for async fallback: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/812
- Raw trace sample export (s3): s3://redwood-prod-traces/2026-01-25_to_2026-02-01/spectral-cohort-sample.ndjson

Notes to reviewers
This is a working brief — focused on pragmatic short experiments rather than exhaustive root-cause. Please comment inline or ping on #eng-serving-runtime. If we agree on the canary configs, I will open the rollout plan doc and schedule a 30-minute sync to align infra and SRE.
